core_obligations: Apply the finite type descent lemma to see that the module is of finite type (proof lines 2195-2196).

Use Nakayama's lemma to establish that the module is generated by r sections in a neighbourhood of a point if and only if the dimension over the residue field of its fibre at that point is at most r (proof lines 2196-2199).

Choose a member of the covering and a point of it mapping to the chosen point, and identify the dimension of the fibre of the module at the point with the dimension of the fibre of the pulled back module at the preimage (proof lines 2200-2202).
Bound the latter by r using the hypothesis on the pullback, and conclude (proof lines 2202-2204).
proof_roadmap: Nakayama: generation by r sections becomes a dimension bound (proof lines 2196-2199).
Transfer the dimension bound along the covering (proof lines 2200-2202).
Conclude with the hypothesis on the pullback (proof lines 2202-2204).
difficulty_reason: Given an fpqc covering of a scheme and a quasi-coherent module whose pullback to each member of the covering is locally generated by r sections, the lemma asserts that the module itself is locally generated by r sections (statement lines 2184-2192). The proof is a numerical criterion argument. It first gets finite type for the module by the descent lemma for finite type, and then uses Nakayama's lemma to replace the property of being generated by r sections near a point by the inequality that the dimension over the residue field of the fibre of the module at that point is at most r (proof lines 2194-2199). The remaining step is to relate that dimension at a point of the base to the corresponding dimension at a preimage point in the covering, which is where the fpqc hypothesis is used, and the hypothesis on the pullback bounds the latter by r, giving the result (proof lines 2200-2204). The claim is H2: the reduction of a generation condition to a dimension inequality through Nakayama's lemma is the substance, and the equality of the two dimensions across a point and its preimage has to be seen.
